clue.text: Associate going to and fro at church

parts.note: the clue word taken as written

indicators.note: going to and then fro means the little word at is written once forwards and then once backwards

parts.note: the same clue word, used again for its backwards trip

explanation.surface: Someone linked to a church who is forever bustling back and forth there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to and fro' makes the one word 'at' do a round trip, forwards then backwards, before the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate one thing with another is to connect or join it, a verb sense shared with fasten on.

clue.text: Rates a little page and then shows appreciation

parts.note: P is the short form of page
to praise is to show appreciation

explanation.surface: A young page boy rates something and then voices approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little page' gives the abbreviation P, not a young servant.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the value of something is to rate or value it, as a valuer does.

clue.text: Push a number into a sailing man's transport

indicators.note: into means these pieces go inside the sailor

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to ram is to push hard
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Shoving a figure into a sailor's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: C is a Roman numeral, so 'a number' can give it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a street vehicle running on rails, a form of public transport.

clue.text: The person one's told has in fact done badly

indicators.note: badly done means made wrongly, so the letters of in fact done are rearranged

explanation.surface: The friend you confided in has, it turns out, behaved poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IN FACT DONE; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted friend to whom secrets are confided is the person one tells everything.

clue.text: A reading may disclose the removal of unwanted moisture

indicators.note: the words a reading may be opened up and rearranged to show a different word

explanation.surface: Checking a meter could reveal how well damp is being dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may disclose' tells you to rearrange the eight letters of A READING. 'A reading' looks like a meter reading in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying away surplus water from soil or buildings is what pipes and ditches do, the process the word names.

clue.text: Compensated — with a new outfit?

definitions.meaning: made amends for a wrong, as a grievance is put right

explanation.surface: Paid back, and given fresh clothes into the bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as re-dressed, dressed again.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong put right has been set right, and a person clothed again has been dressed anew.

clue.text: Irritation caused by coppers evacuating the sports ground

indicators.note: the coppers move out of the ground, so their letter is removed

parts.note: a pitch is a playing field for sports
P stands for pence, coins once made of copper

explanation.surface: Police clearing a stadium cause annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like police but means copper coins, pence, P.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritation of the skin is an urge to scratch, an itch.

clue.text: Hard worker accepting a far from reasonable rise

indicators.note: the worker takes in the other letters, accepting them inside

parts.note: an ant is the usual crossword worker

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: mad means irrational, far from reasonable

explanation.surface: A hard worker takes on a wildly unreasonable pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' reads upwards, so 'a' plus the word for unreasonable is turned round (DAMA) before the worker takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding and firmly set is what hard means here, a rock-like resolve.

clue.text: Newspaper leader about people effecting reform

indicators.note: about means round, so the leader goes round the people

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the head of a newspaper
men means people

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial about people bringing about change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper leader' looks like an editorial, but is the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or amend a text is to reform it, the sense of improving by changes.

clue.text: Caught and bolted a quantity of fish

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to bolt is to run off, so bolted is ran

explanation.surface: A fish catch was caught and then got away.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught is a cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish, is a cran.

clue.text: Scheming individual is smoother without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a planer is a tool that smooths wood
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A schemer is a tool for smoothing that lacks any sharp edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: PLANER sits outside N. A compass point is a common crossword source of N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plots and organises ahead is a person who draws up schemes, here a schemer.

clue.text: Brook: no opposition when in office?

definitions.text: Brook: no opposition when in office?

parts.words: Brook: no opposition when in office?
parts.note: to brook no opposition is to lay down the law; the question mark hints at a ruler in office, or a boss giving letters to a typist

explanation.surface: A demand that a stream should face no opposition once elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook' is not a stream but the verb meaning tolerate; one who brooks no opposition simply gives orders. In an office it also means reading words aloud for a secretary to write.
explanation.definitionFit: To order people about without accepting argument is to command, and giving words for a secretary to take down is the office sense.

clue.text: A man with lots to offer

definitions.text: A man with lots to offer

parts.words: A man with lots to offer
parts.note: the lots are numbered items at a sale, which this person offers to bidders

explanation.surface: A generous, gifted man who has plenty to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like plenty, but means the numbered items put up at a sale room.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs a sale by bidding offers each numbered lot in turn to the room.

clue.text: Deposited money to provide support

parts.note: L stands for pound, the British currency (from Latin libra)
aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Money was put in the bank to help someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from the Latin libra, as in the old British £sd currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To have deposited something is to have put it down, as a hen does with an egg.

clue.text: A simple plot

parts.note: simples are medicinal plants, so a plot of them is a patch of ground grown with them

explanation.surface: A story line with no complications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like an adjective, but simples are old medicinal herbs; 'plot' is a garden bed, not a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Simples are old medicinal plants, so a patch growing them is a garden of herbs.

clue.text: Help firm to acquire the right vehicle

indicators.note: a firm word taking in other letters, the way a company acquires something

parts.note: set means firm, as a jelly that has set
R is the abbreviation for right
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A domestic help needs the company to buy them a suitable van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective, as when a jelly is firm; 'to acquire' puts the right-hand letter and the vehicle inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic employee who assists in a household is a help, an old term for a maid.

clue.text: Most exciting thing about running water

indicators.note: about means round, so the thing goes round the water

parts.note: the clue word taken as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: The most exciting object near a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'Most exciting' stands for a plain adjective, not a superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly exciting and stirring is what the adjective conveys, a gripping sensation.

clue.text: An officer in out-and-out retreat

indicators.note: the officer goes in the word for out-and-out

parts.note: sheer means utter or out-and-out, as in sheer folly
LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer caught up in a complete rout of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' suggests an army withdrawal but is a noun for a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of refuge or cover where one can withdraw for safety is a retreat.

clue.text: Boom in non-crease materials

indicators.note: materials made from these letters, as non-crease fabrics are worked into new form

explanation.surface: A boom in wrinkle-free fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom' looks like a trade surge but is a deep resounding sound; 'materials' rearranges NON-CREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep reverberating sound echoing on is the quality of a boom.

clue.text: No tears affected the American politician

indicators.note: affected means altered or changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American politician was not moved to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Senate is a type of elected politician in Washington.

clue.text: There's no way drink can be a cure-all

parts.note: the clue word taken as written
ST, short for street, is a way
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: No path offers alcohol as a cure for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the abbreviation for street, a common crossword way.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy or panacea claiming to heal every ill is a cure-all.

clue.text: Knights holding acknowledgement of indebtedness suspect

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: a monarch dubs a man a knight, so dubs means knights as a verb
an IOU, 'I owe you', is a written note admitting a debt

explanation.surface: Knights with a debt note are viewed with suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knights' is a verb here: a monarch knights someone by touching their shoulder with a sword, the old ceremony of dubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to doubt and not to be trusted is questionable, a sense of the adjective suspect.

clue.text: Artistry when at the crease

parts.note: a crease in cricket is where the batsman stands, but here it is the fold in a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: Skilful batting while at the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease in cricket is the line a batsman stands at, but here it is a fold in a sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes is an art of creases.

clue.text: Some cereals only are allowed in addition

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only certain breakfast cereals are permitted as extras.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'are allowed in addition' as the definition, but the answer means only 'in addition'; 'are allowed' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: As well or besides is the meaning shared by in addition and the answer, an adverb of adding.

clue.text: Article on a jerk, an old buffoon

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tic is a jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A clown on a twitch, an old buffoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like a fool, but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage this noun meant a clown or grotesque performer, a buffoon.

clue.text: Writing a story, people can cause estrangement

parts.note: a story is a fib, a lie
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Inventing tales can turn a whole people against one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing a story' is a link phrase introducing A plus a story in the sense of a lie, then NATION for people.
explanation.definitionFit: Making someone feel isolated or hostile is to drive them apart, an act of estrangement.

clue.text: Update issue

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for date is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a date is a time

explanation.surface: Publish the latest edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Update' splits as up + date: date gives TIME, and up turns it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it out or give it off, as fumes are released.

clue.text: This Italian place is in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in means the word is goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania
the clue word taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian town that turns out to be in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a namesake town in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous for its leaning tower, this is a city in Tuscany, Italy.

clue.text: The limitations of rail travel

parts.note: the limits of a railway journey are the end stations where the line stops

explanation.surface: Complaining about the drawbacks of going by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitations' looks like drawbacks, but means the physical end points of the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: End-of-line stations, plural of the Latin word for boundary, are where railway journeys stop.

clue.text: Inspired attraction in a hostelry

indicators.note: the attraction goes in the hostelry

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
a draw is an attraction, something that pulls in a crowd

explanation.surface: An inspired idea for drawing customers into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' is not the creative sense but the breathing one: breath drawn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Breath that has been breathed into the lungs has been taken in, the literal sense of inspired.

clue.text: Organising a camping expedition

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Planning a trip to go and pitch tents somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organising' rearranges A CAMPING.
explanation.definitionFit: A military operation or series of manoeuvres is a campaign, an organised expedition.

clue.text: Not to be compared with a French relish

parts.note: un is the French for a
to relish is to enjoy or like

explanation.surface: A French condiment that has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a condiment but is the verb, LIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that differ completely are dissimilar and cannot be compared.
